situation.text: PST raised the sabotage threat on 12 November and expects Russian intelligence to try sabotage in Norway within a year, most likely against the defence industry and its suppliers. A Russian analyst has already called Kongsberg's plants legitimate targets. NASAMS sensors now watch for drones at Kirkenes, and the UK has agreed to buy three Norwegian-built mine-hunting motherships.

Nordic defence ministers agreed in Oslo on 12 November to start work on a Nordic defence agreement so forces can move and fight across borders. Finland reported a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland on 11 November, as Ukrainian drones hit targets around St Petersburg. Sweden warns of Russian attempts at destructive cyberattacks on power, water and heating systems.

Russia keeps up nightly drone and missile attacks on Kyiv, Odesa, Rivne and energy sites, while fighting is fiercest around Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk. Ukraine has hit five of Russia's largest refineries since 30 October. Air defence remains the bottleneck: interceptor missiles are short, and a speed limit on Starshield links makes it harder to catch jet-powered drones.

A drone from Belarus crossed Lithuania on 11 November and NATO jets failed twice to shoot it down, while Spain used helicopters against drones over Romania for the first time. Russia's hybrid campaign of sabotage, cyberattacks and drone incursions goes on, and Moscow now offers bilateral non-aggression pacts to single NATO states. The EU agreed a EUR 3.1 bn defence budget for 2027.

news.title: Syncrolift wins NOK 940 m contract for world's largest shiplift at a US naval yard
news.summary: The Norwegian firm, part of Nekkar, calls it the largest contract in its history. It more than doubles its order backlog. Norwegian maritime suppliers are finding a way into the US naval build-up.

news.title: PST raises sabotage threat in Norway
news.summary: PST expects Russian intelligence to attempt sabotage in Norway in the coming year, often through hired proxies. The defence industry, defence-related firms and their suppliers, such as logistics companies, are the most likely targets. Methods include arson, explosives and drones. Every defence startup should review site security and report anything unusual to PST.

news.title: Nordic countries start work on a Nordic defence agreement
news.summary: Norway, Denmark, Finland, Sweden and Iceland agreed at the NORDEFCO meeting in Oslo to build a legal and political framework for closer defence cooperation in peace, crisis and war. The aim is to let forces move and operate across borders with fewer obstacles. Ministers also welcomed the industry-led Nordic Compass initiative.

news.title: UK to buy three Norwegian-built mine-hunting motherships
news.summary: The deal is worth about GBP 90 m (NOK 1.14 bn), with an option for three more ships, and falls under the same framework as Norway's British frigates. The ships will carry uncrewed mine-clearance systems and join the P1118 standardized vessel programme. Deliveries start around 2030–31.

news.title: UK defence software firm Arondite to invest NOK 430 m in Norway
news.summary: Arondite, maker of the Cobalt mission management platform used by British forces, opens its first office outside the UK in Oslo. The investment is spread over five years and the office is led by former officer and Visma executive Eirik Friise. A new, well-funded competitor and partner for Norwegian C2 and software startups.

news.title: Nammo moves beyond warheads to supply complete drones
news.summary: Nammo, so far known for drone warheads, will now supply complete drones. That puts a Norwegian prime in the drone market where startups compete and partner.

news.title: Russian analyst calls Kongsberg plants legitimate targets
news.summary: The remark follows Russian claims of shooting down four Rusty Dagger missiles made by Zone 5, a US company 90% owned by Kongsberg. Defence suppliers should treat physical and cyber security of their sites as a real issue.

news.title: Norway's NORDSEC cluster and France's EDEN sign cooperation agreement
news.summary: The MoU covers knowledge exchange, joint projects and meeting places. EDEN represents more than 280 French defence SMEs. A French delegation visits Norway in 2027.

news.title: Danish navy memo: six frigates needed to meet NATO targets
news.summary: According to an internal memo seen by DR, the frigates would form the core of a hybrid fleet of crewed ships and drones. That points to Danish demand for naval drones and the systems that tie them together.

news.title: Finland reports strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland
news.summary: The Finnish Defence Forces detected a strike on a Russian warship on 11 November and say the situation is stable. Militarnyi reports that Ukraine hit the Buyan-M missile ship Naro-Fominsk near Gogland island. The war is now reaching Nordic waters.

news.title: Sweden plans to sell up to 20 CB90 combat boats to France
news.summary: The government-to-government deal is slated for 2027 and includes training and support equipment. The government is asking parliament for approval in its interim budget.

news.title: Missile maker Covenant signs more NATO deals after Denmark goes first
news.summary: Denmark ordered Covenant's Anthem strike missile in October as launch customer, and the minister says it was the best option on price and range. Covenant says more NATO countries have since bought it and aims to build 1,000 missiles in 2027. A sign that Nordic buyers will back new, unproven suppliers when price and speed are right.

news.title: Nordic defence industry associations urge governments to act
news.summary: The Danish, Finnish, Norwegian and Swedish associations back the Nordic Compass Defence initiative from Ericsson, Kongsberg, Nokia, Patria, Saab and Terma. They ask for fewer cross-border barriers and measurable demand signals. The Nordic base counts about 1,650 companies, mostly SMEs.

news.title: Elisa and Sensofusion launch drone detection joint venture
news.summary: The Finnish telecom operator and counter-drone company, who already ran a border drone-detection trial together, are forming a joint venture.

news.title: Nordic Air Defence hires former UK armed forces minister, prepares round
news.summary: The Stockholm interceptor-drone startup hired James Heappey as chief growth officer and a former Helsing manager. Its K100 is close to testing in Ukraine. It lost SEK 33.7 m in 2025 and is raising to start production.

news.title: Nordic defence ministers meet in Oslo, 11–12 November
news.summary: Norway hosts NORDEFCO as 2026 chair. Agenda: Nordic cooperation within NATO and total defence. Press briefing on 12 November.

news.title: UFORCE raises USD 700 m at a USD 6 bn valuation
news.summary: The Ukrainian maker of bomber and interceptor drones, MAGURA sea drones and ground robots raised a Series A led by the UK's National Wealth Fund and Valor Equity Partners. Lakestar, Shield Capital and the US–Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund also joined.

news.title: Starshield speed limit hampers interception of Russian jet drones
news.summary: Ukrainian troops report a systematic cap of about 161 km/h on Starshield links along the whole front. Zelenskyy says interceptor drones cannot reach the speed needed to catch jet-powered drones. Kyiv is seeking clarification from the US. Shows the risk of depending on one foreign comms provider.

news.title: Ukraine and the Netherlands work on ballistic missile interception
news.summary: The two projects are FREYJA, expected to show first results next year, and Bliksem, which starts simulation tests at the end of this year. Patriot output is too small when one Russian attack on Kyiv can involve about 40 ballistic missiles.

news.title: Fedorov co-founds anti-drone missile company
news.summary: Former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov and Lasar's Group founder Pavlo Yelizarov launched Mission Defense Partners. It builds low-cost missiles up to 15 km with radar seekers and interceptor drones. Palantir's Alex Karp is reported as its first big investor.

news.title: Two Ukrainian companies win NATO tenders for the first time
news.summary: They won through an NSPA mechanism that lets Ukrainian firms join NATO procurement and find partners in member states. The companies were not named.

news.title: Italy runs out of Aster missiles for Ukraine's SAMP/T
news.summary: Interceptor stocks are the weak point of Ukraine's air defence, which keeps demand high for cheaper interceptors.

news.title: Drones hit Russia's Ust-Luga port
news.summary: A drone attack sparked a fire at the strategic Baltic port, showing Ukraine's long-range drone reach.

news.title: Russia–Ukraine–US talks in Abu Dhabi
news.summary: Nearly four hours of US-mediated talks, while the armies remain largely deadlocked on the front.

news.title: Moscow offers non-aggression pacts to individual NATO states
news.summary: A Russian foreign ministry official floated bilateral non-aggression deals at a Moscow security forum. Russia's chief negotiator said a new European security architecture was the main topic of the Abu Dhabi talks.

news.title: Spanish NH90 helicopters used against drones over Romania for the first time
news.summary: Spain's air policing detachment scrambled two NH90s after unidentified drones were detected on 6 November. Its commander says helicopters add to fighter jets but do not replace them. NATO is still improvising cheaper ways to stop drones.

news.title: NATO jets twice fail to shoot down drone over Lithuania
news.summary: A drone from Belarus crossed Lithuania, passing over Kaunas. Jets missed twice near Biržai and missile debris fell there. Its type and payload are unknown. A clear case for cheap detection and interception.

news.title: EU agrees EUR 3.1 bn defence and security budget for 2027
news.summary: The budget includes EUR 650 m from the Ukraine Support Loan. It is the last year of the current long-term budget; talks on 2028–2034 are contentious.

news.title: Dutch WARDEN air defence missile to be built with Ukrainian firms
news.summary: Guardian Dynamics leads a consortium with Demcon, Axient and TNO on missiles with 5, 10 and 20 km range for existing launchers. Ukrainian companies will make components and join tests from 2027.

news.title: Bundeswehr bans Chinese drones and cars from military bases
news.summary: The ban is driven by espionage fears. Products free of Chinese parts gain an edge with European militaries.

news.title: How Russia wages hybrid war on Europe
news.summary: Arson, sabotage, cyberattacks and armed drone incursions aimed at countries that back Kyiv.

news.title: Newsroom bomb threats follow wave of European flight hoaxes
news.summary: A new pattern of disruptive hoaxes adds to pressure on European infrastructure and services.

press.title: Work begins on a Nordic defence agreement
press.summary: Norway, Denmark, Finland, Sweden and Iceland will start work on a Nordic defence agreement, agreed at the NORDEFCO ministers' meeting in Oslo on 11–12 November. The goal is closer cooperation that strengthens NATO deterrence and lets Nordic forces operate seamlessly across borders. Ministers discussed a legal and political framework for peace, crisis and war, and want to remove practical and legal obstacles to moving forces. The Nordic countries together have about 250 modern fighter jets, 145 surface vessels and 100,000 personnel in peacetime. No timeline was given.
press.startup: The release does not mention procurement, but common rules for moving forces point toward more shared exercises, logistics and systems (inference). Products that work across all Nordic forces will have a bigger market.
press.tldr: Nordic forces are integrating; sell to all five, not one.

press.title: MoD asks agencies to prepare corrective actions after audit
press.summary: Riksrevisjonen found that the 2025 accounts of Forsvaret, FFI and FMA may contain material errors, and could not give an opinion on Forsvarsbygg. The MoD has ordered concrete action plans with reporting requirements. Forsvaret must strengthen inventory control with an annual stock-count plan, FMA risks booking purchases in the wrong fiscal year, and Forsvarsbygg gets an external review of its financial management.
press.startup: Expect stricter documentation on deliveries, invoice timing and inventory traceability when you sell to FMA or Forsvaret. There may be demand for inventory, traceability and financial-control tools.
press.tldr: Expect stricter paperwork when you deliver to FMA and Forsvaret.

press.title: Nordic defence ministers' meeting in Oslo
press.summary: Norway chairs NORDEFCO in 2026 and hosts the Nordic defence ministers in Oslo on 11–12 November. Topics include stronger Nordic defence cooperation within NATO and total defence. A press briefing is held on 12 November.
press.startup: Nordic joint procurement and shared test arenas are growing. A product that fits several Nordic forces is easier to scale than one built for Norway only.
press.tldr: Build for all the Nordic forces, not Norway alone.

press.titleNo: Norge har mottatt det første amfibiske bro- og fergesystemet M3N til Hæren
press.title: First M3N amphibious bridge and ferry system delivered to the Army
press.summary: FMA delivered the first M3N amphibious bridging and ferry system to the Army, giving better mobility across rivers and fjords.
press.startup: Limited direct relevance. Shows the Army's focus on mobility and logistics, where autonomy and maintenance tools can add value.
press.tldr: Low direct relevance; shows focus on Army mobility.

press.titleNo: Forsvarsmateriell inviterer norske verft til konkurranse om nye fartøy til Sjøforsvaret
press.title: Norwegian yards invited to compete for new Navy vessels
press.summary: National prequalification for up to 28 standardized vessels for the Navy, Coast Guard and allies: up to 10 ocean-going and 18 coastal. Split into two contracts to widen Norwegian participation. Vessels must be built in Norway; hulls may be built abroad. Apply via Mercell (documents, timeline, deadline); the notice is also on Doffin. Only a limited number of qualified suppliers will be invited to bid. Contact: forsvarsmateriell@fma.no, +47 23 09 30 03.
press.startup: Startups will not build ships, but autonomy, sensors, C2 software, drone hangars and maintenance tech can ride along as subsuppliers. Talk to the yards that prequalify.
press.tldr: Big ship deal: get in as a subsupplier through the yards.

press.titleNo: Regjeringen styrker norske investeringer i Ukraina med 1 milliard kroner
press.title: NOK 1 bn to strengthen Norwegian investment in Ukraine
press.summary: A NOK 1 bn framework over three years, taken from the military part of the Nansen programme and placed under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries. Investinor manages it by investing in Norwegian-based funds that back Ukrainian defence companies. Investinor picks the funds; the fund managers pick the companies. Direct co-investments may follow.
press.startup: Norwegian–Ukrainian joint ventures and Ukrainian partners of Norwegian startups may become investable through these funds. Talk to Investinor and Norwegian defence-tech fund managers early.
press.tldr: New NOK 1 bn fund route makes Norwegian–Ukrainian ventures easier to finance.

press.titleNo: Styrker evnen til å oppdage droner i Finnmark
press.title: Stronger drone detection in Finnmark
press.summary: The Armed Forces place air-surveillance sensors (NASAMS) in Kirkenes to detect and warn of drones in the border area. About 30 soldiers from the Garrison of Sør-Varanger will be stationed there through the year. The deployment is preventive. Police enforce drone rules and the Armed Forces assist on request.
press.startup: Clear demand signal for low-cost drone detection and early warning in Arctic conditions. No tender is attached, but this is a use case to pitch to the Home Guard, FFI and FMA.
press.tldr: Clear demand for cheap Arctic drone detection, but no tender yet.

press.title: New Operational Support Command (FOSK) from 1 January 2027
press.summary: FLO and the Armed Forces Medical Services merge into the Norwegian Armed Forces Operational Support Command (FOSK) on 1 January 2027. FOSK supports other units with resources from the defence sector and the wider total defence system.
press.startup: A new buyer organisation for logistics, maintenance and medical solutions. Map who owns what in FOSK before 2027.
press.tldr: A new logistics and medical buyer from January 2027.

press.title: Four-year military engineering degree proposed
press.summary: The government proposes a four-year military engineering education and more flexible engineering studies to meet the defence sector's need for technical staff.
press.startup: Competition for engineers will grow. Partnerships with the Defence University College and student projects can be a recruitment channel.
press.tldr: Hiring engineers will get harder; partner with the military schools early.

press.titleNo: Forsvarsmateriell signaliserer konkurransemodell for standardiserte fartøy
press.title: Market signal: competition model for standardized vessels (P1118)
press.summary: Up to 20 ocean-going vessels planned for Norway, the UK and Lithuania, split into one contract for up to 14 naval vessels and one for up to 6 coast guard vessels. One bidder should not win both. Target: contracts in 2027 and first delivery in 2030. The signal is preliminary and may change.
press.startup: Market signals are FMA's early warning to industry. Read P1118 now if your product belongs on a ship; integration slots are decided early.
press.tldr: Contracts in 2027, first ships in 2030; integration slots are decided now.

press.title: Armed Forces modernise Nødnett radio terminals
press.summary: 1,320 new Nødnett terminals (Motorola MXP600), about 650 replacing first-generation units. The Army's 280 terminals come through TC Connect; the Home Guard gets 290. The goal is better direct communication with civilian emergency services and Nordic partners.
press.startup: Total defence means military and civilian systems must talk to each other. Interoperability with Nødnett and TETRA is a plus for comms and C2 products.
press.tldr: Make your comms and C2 products work with civilian emergency radio.

readings.title: The “Battle of Norway”
readings.publisher: Sahaidachnyi Security Center, supported by Buntar Aerospace
readings.summary: Argues that the most likely attack on Norway is not a ground invasion of Finnmark but a 'Battle of Britain' in the drone era: mass drone and missile strikes, sea drones and sabotage against energy, subsea cables and logistics. It sees a threat window of 2027–2029, while most Norwegian programmes mature in 2029–2036. Biggest gaps: counter-drone and ballistic defence, sabotage detection at sea, tactical electronic warfare and manpower in Finnmark. Recommends a standing Ukraine–Norway capability partnership, starting with a Home Guard counter-drone shield.
readings.tldr: Norway's real gap is cheap mass defence against drones and sabotage, and Ukraine can help close it fast.

readings.title: Sabotage threat in Norway raised
readings.summary: PST's updated assessment says Russian intelligence will likely attempt sabotage in Norway in the coming year, mostly through proxies. The defence industry, defence-related businesses and their suppliers are the most likely targets, followed by critical infrastructure such as energy. PST asks companies to know their normal picture and report anything that deviates from it.
readings.tldr: Defence startups and their suppliers are now named sabotage targets; secure your sites.

readings.title: National Threat Assessment 2026
readings.summary: Russian and Chinese intelligence activity is expected to rise, with focus on military targets, Ukraine support, the High North and critical infrastructure. Essential context for anyone selling security or surveillance tech.
readings.tldr: Russian and Chinese spying in Norway is rising; expect stricter security demands on suppliers.

readings.title: Fokus 2026
readings.summary: The intelligence service's annual open assessment of the external threats to Norway, with Russia's military posture in the north at the centre.
readings.tldr: Russia's military power in the north remains the core threat to Norway.

readings.title: Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries (2014–2026)
readings.summary: Official spending, share of GDP, equipment share and personnel for all allies. The numbers on the map above come from here.
readings.tldr: Every ally but Slovenia now spends 2%+ of GDP; the money is there.

readings.title: Forsvarsløftet: long-term plan for the defence sector 2025–2036
readings.summary: The cross-party plan behind about NOK 600 bn in extra defence spending over 12 years. Tells you what Norway will buy and when.
readings.tldr: NOK 600 bn extra over 12 years: this is Norway's shopping list.

readings.title: Meld. St. 33 (2024–2025): status of the long-term plan
readings.summary: Progress, challenges and risks in delivering the long-term plan. Useful to see where programmes are late and where faster solutions are needed.
readings.tldr: Several programmes are late; that is where faster solutions are welcome.

readings.title: Roadmap for increased production capacity in the defence industry
readings.summary: The government's roadmap for scaling Norwegian defence production. Relevant for manufacturers and suppliers to the primes.
readings.tldr: Norway wants more production at home; manufacturers and subsuppliers benefit.

readings.title: New law on defence and security procurement (report)
readings.summary: Proposal for a new procurement law for defence and security. Shapes how startups can be bought from in the future.
readings.tldr: Procurement rules are being rewritten; watch how they treat small firms.

readings.title: National Security Strategy
readings.summary: Norway's first national security strategy, tying together defence, total defence, economy and technology.
readings.tldr: Security now spans defence, economy and technology, which widens the dual-use market.

readings.title: Readiness Roadmap 2030
readings.summary: The EU's four flagships, including the European Drone Defence Initiative and Eastern Flank Watch, with milestones to 2030.
readings.tldr: The EU wants a working drone shield and eastern flank watch by 2027–2030.

readings.title: White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030
readings.summary: The ReArm Europe plan, up to EUR 800 bn, and the SAFE loan instrument. Explains where EU defence money flows.
readings.tldr: Up to EUR 800 bn in EU defence money; SAFE loans favour European suppliers.

readings.title: Defence spending: who is doing what? (July 2026)
readings.summary: Country-by-country analysis of NATO's 2026 figures and the path to the Hague 3.5% + 1.5% target.
readings.tldr: Spending is rising everywhere, fastest on the eastern flank and in the Nordics.

readings.title: Russia's hybrid warfare campaign in Europe
readings.summary: Briefing on sabotage, cyberattacks, disinformation and drone incursions across Europe.
readings.tldr: Sabotage and drone incursions are the new normal, creating demand for protection of critical infrastructure.

readings.title: Ukraine Support Tracker
readings.summary: Tracks military, financial and humanitarian aid to Ukraine by country.
readings.tldr: Shows who funds Ukraine and how much, so you can see where the money is.
